main_text.p: videndus est inquit, Athenæus, Plutar-chus, Baptista Porta, & alii, qui de Mu-sicæ effectu scripserunt. Veteres sanè, inquit, ad concitandos in bellum animos, ufi sunt Musicâ, ut Lacedæmo-nii, qui versus Tytæi & Pindari decantabant. Et erat Phrygium genus, inquit, ad hanc rem aptum. Timotheus Musicus Phrygio instigavit Alexandrum ad arma: Cromaticum ad mollitiem erat comparatum remissionemque animi; Doricum ad castitatem & prudentiam; Lydium ad intelleƈtus acumen. De Chaˈ-meleone Pontico & Achille memorat Athenæus, quòd Musica sedaverint concitatam iram. Sed in his saltem est aliqua declaratio, inquit, quia Iracundi datâ occasiunculâ aliquâ, qualis est gravis & severus sonus, facilè ad iram vertuntur, & pro confuso moventur, veluti Plutarchus, qui auditis modis, qui Harmatii vocantur, ab Antigenide decantatis, hostem ex amico affidente fecit, irruens in ipsum cum impetu.

page.notes: Marginal left-edge marks are printed signs, not legible notes; several words are italic or set with a reference mark ("ˈ"). Some ligature-like letters (e.g. "Chaˈ-") and the hyphenated "Chaˈmeleone" are uncertain; the word "meleone" begins a new line with the hyphen lost in the scan. The top-of-page fragment is treated as a continuation.
